title: Bounded result JSON retains host compatibility and projection responsibilities
observed_need: Expose a stable result document to mncs-actions and future Forge without losing typed native values or structured diagnostics.
current_language_behavior: Native assertions, suite verdicts, retained execution values, process-outcome classification, subprocess-fallback execution adjudication, the family-check path CheckResult policy projection, bounded run_id plus per-test lineage digests, per-test canonical execution/observation JSON construction for ordinary bounded string/null fields, ArtifactStore payload/file digests through 65,536 bytes, compiler/source/manifest provenance file digests through the ArtifactStore bounded file adapter, using one MNCS request up to 14,336 bytes and retained MNCS streaming through 512 KiB after warm-up, and public result JSON formatting for bounded JSON value trees are MNCS-owned. The run-identity app constructs canonical JSON for bounded inputs; Python projects typed identity fields and retains compact-JSON compatibility for out-of-contract inputs. The result-identity batch app handles up to 16 payloads, 64 chunks, 65,536 bytes, and the 8,000,000-step limit. The stream app carries native SHA-256 state across ArtifactStore calls of at most 14,336 bytes each and at most five calls per artifact. After three bounded native application hashes in one ArtifactStore, a retained mncs-embed session calls the same pure MNCS identity and SHA-256 functions for payloads and artifact files through 512 KiB; provenance hashing uses the existing ArtifactStore stream for files above 14,336 bytes; each retained window contains at most 14,336 bytes and one MNCS function call. The final window finalizes in that same call; the retained Python adapter no longer calls SHA-256 initialization or finalization directly. Larger artifacts and inputs before warm-up use host hashlib; failed embedding also falls back to the established host or native-app path. Python reads files, enumerates and sorts directories, hashes library leaves, sends bounded chunks, writes artifacts, and supervises processes; the MNCS library-tree identity application folds up to 128 ordered path and leaf-digest records; filesystem traversal, leaf reads, and the explicit host fallback remain in the adapter; source/provenance files above 65,536 bytes before warm-up, above 512 KiB, or after embedding failure retain host hashing; the Rust bootstrap CLI retains its JSON and artifact boundaries. The public serializer sorts object keys, escapes and indents values, and emits the trailing newline. Documents through 16,300 bytes use the single-call application; documents through 32,684 bytes use up to 32 continuation calls of at most 8,192 JSON bytes each. Pages may stop before a whole value when its conservative size bound would cross the page limit, leaving page capacity unused; the window application carries native SHA-256 state across pages. The ordinary compile-failure Test runner also now serializes its 8,042-byte, 198-node result through test-public-result-json-window.json within the existing 8,000,000-step budget after the native serializer stopped scanning unused fixed-width JSON writer bytes.
why_insufficient: The bounded public serializer accepts at most 512 values, depth 63, 64 children per object, 256-byte keys, 1,024-byte scalar text, and 32,684 output bytes. Larger or unsupported values retain the compatibility path. Python still performs typed value projection, reassembles native UTF-8-safe pages, and writes public documents. The subprocess native-stream path remains capped at 65,536 bytes: the exact-65,536-byte payload/file differential test uses five native app updates per artifact. After three bounded native app hashes, the retained session handles artifacts through 512 KiB in windows of at most 14,336 bytes. Differential tests cover a 512 KiB payload and a 393,233-byte compiler artifact against independent hashlib digests. An uncapped self-suite run reached the real 13 MB compiler artifacts and was interrupted after 4:21 while the runner used about 150 MB RSS and remained CPU-bound; this run did not pass and provides no performance claim. The retained path is now capped at 512 KiB, with host streaming hashlib for larger artifacts, before warm-up, or when embedding is unavailable. The complete cross-repository evidence protocol and out-of-contract run-identity projection remain outside the native application surface. Python retains typed value projection, filesystem access and traversal, per-file library leaf hashes, host fallback for source/provenance files above 65,536 bytes before warm-up, above 512 KiB, or when retained embedding is unavailable; inputs through 65,536 bytes retain the native-app fallback, and compatibility behavior for unsupported or over-bound inputs. The Rust bootstrap CLI retains its JSON and artifact boundaries. A normal compile-pass integration check exceeded Control's MCP request deadline at 2:07 while the first implementation routed library trees through repeated native hashes; it was stopped, did not pass, and provides no performance claim. The final ordered library-tree identity fold uses MNCS for up to 128 entries within the 65,536-byte request bound; filesystem traversal and leaf hashes remain host responsibilities, with the host digest as an explicit and reported fallback. After library hashing was restored to host, a second local compile-pass check remained CPU-bound at 3:35 and was terminated without a result. The slow phase is unknown; neither integration attempt passed. A new ordinary-runner reproduction isolated one budget failure to the JSON string and integer emitters scanning all 64 slots of json_emit.Writer.buf when only len bytes were live. Those loops now use the live byte range; the 8,042-byte result completes in the native window application within 8,000,000 steps and byte-matches an independent Python JSON golden. Broader input bounds and compatibility handling for unsupported values or actual native failures remain.
minimal_reproducer: tools/mncs_test.py::ResultIdentityEmbedHasher.digest_chunks sends bounded requests to Test-owned MNCS stream transitions; the final update returns the finalized SHA-256 digest in the same call. tests/test_artifact_hashing.py::test_artifact_store_hashes_large_payloads_in_a_retained_mncs_session checks empty and exact-14,336-byte streams plus independent digests for a 512 KiB payload and a 393,233-byte file, confirms one transition per window with no direct SHA-256 init/finalize calls, confirms only three warm-up hashes launch the app, and verifies session cleanup. test_artifact_store_hashes_native_stream_limit_in_five_updates checks exact 65,536-byte payload and file inputs against independent digests using five updates each. tests/test_artifact_hashing.py::test_artifact_store_keeps_large_files_on_host_after_session_warmup confirms the 512 KiB ceiling remains in force after the native session threshold is met. The provenance differential test warms the retained session, hashes bounded compiler, source, and manifest files through ArtifactStore, compares every digest with independent hashlib, and verifies the runner source uses the retained MNCS stream and the bounded directory fixture proves that MNCS owns the library-tree fold while host code retains per-file reads. tests/test_public_result_json.py::test_compile_failure_runner_keeps_medium_public_result_native runs the ordinary compile-failure runner, records native application outcomes, rejects any compatibility serializer call for TestResult/CheckResult, and compares the emitted document to an independent JSON golden.
desired_direction: Extend the bounded native serializer and streaming identity capabilities through real consumers, while moving common text, collection, and typed-value projection mechanisms into reusable MNCS stdlib interfaces where migration requirements support them. Keep application policy and platform filesystem/process access at their existing ownership boundaries.
workaround: The MNCS test-check-result-projection application owns CheckResult policy and reference construction; test-lineage-identity constructs and hashes ordinary per-test execution/observation JSON; test-run-identity constructs and hashes bounded canonical run identities; test-result-identity hashes bounded payload batches; test-result-identity-stream carries native SHA-256 state through bounded 14,336-byte windows for payloads and files up to 65,536 bytes in at most five calls; after three app-based artifact hashes, ArtifactStore reuses an embedded session through 512 KiB and validates, updates, and finalizes SHA state in one MNCS call per retained window, while preserving host streaming fallback above that bound, before warm-up, or when embedding is unavailable; test-public-result-json serializes values with conservative bounds up to 8,192 bytes, and test-public-result-json-window serializes larger bounded values while carrying SHA-256 state across pages through mncs.std.sha256.v1. The adapter respects native row, field, payload, page, byte, step, and stream-call limits, retains compatibility behavior outside them, and independently checks the final public-document digest; the host compatibility serializer preserves exact output if a bounded native public-result call reports budget_exhausted. manifest_provenance hashes files through 14,336 bytes with one bounded MNCS request and routes files through 512 KiB via ArtifactStore; after session warm-up, runner source uses the retained MNCS stream, while files above 65,536 bytes use host fallback before warm-up or if embedding is unavailable, and files above 512 KiB always use host; inputs through 65,536 bytes retain the native-app fallback. For bounded directories, `mncs.test.library_tree_identity_v1` folds ordered relative names and host-computed leaf SHA-256 values into the final identity. The result names the implementation, while input bounds or application failures select a reported host compatibility fallback. Python keeps filesystem traversal and per-file leaf hashing. Python still projects typed values, reassembles unresolved-message and JSON pages, performs filesystem access and traversal, and falls back to host hashing for oversized or unavailable native inputs before serializing unsupported or over-bound public values. It also retains process supervision, raw diagnostic transport, and explicit Actions/compatibility transport. When the native process-outcome classifier cannot launch after the host observed a process-start failure or timeout, the adapter preserves that direct platform outcome as infrastructure_failure or timeout. The representative ordinary compile-failure result now completes through the MNCS window serializer at 8,000,000 steps and matches the Python JSON golden; compatibility serialization remains available for unsupported or out-of-bound values and native execution failures.
